orders.description: Defendants’ appeal from the May 20, 2014 denial of summary judgment, limited by their brief to actual and constructive notice.
orders.trial_court_action: Denied defendants’ motion for summary judgment dismissing the complaint.

facts.factual_summary: Janice McDonell allegedly slipped and fell on water near the junction of the indoor and outdoor sections of the garden department in defendants’ store. The precise side of that junction is not specified.

legal_issues.finding: Defendants failed to establish that they were unaware of water at the accident location before the fall. This initial-burden failure is not a conclusive finding of actual notice.

Defendants’ own submissions raised factual issues whether the wet floor was visible and apparent long enough for employees to discover and remedy it. No duration or conclusive notice finding is supplied.

The indoor/outdoor junction is coded other rather than forcing an indoor floor or exterior entrance. Plaintiff’s customer status and accident date are unstated. The appealed portion is fully affirmed, label 0. Review is expressly limited to notice, so no creation ruling is inferred. The opinion does not specify evidence formats. evidence.quote: It is hereby ORDERED that the order so appealed from is unanimously affirmed without costs.

Memorandum: Plaintiffs commenced this action seeking damages for injuries allegedly sustained by Janice A. McDonell (plaintiff) when she slipped and fell on water near the junction of the indoor and outdoor sections of the garden department in defendants’ store.
Appeal from an order of the Supreme Court, Erie County (Christopher J. Burns, J.), entered May 20, 2014. The order, insofar as appealed from, denied the motion of defendants for summary judgment.

As limited by their brief, the only issue before us on appeal is whether defendants met their initial burden on their motion of establishing that they did not have actual or constructive notice of the allegedly dangerous condition.

We conclude that defendants failed to meet their burden with respect to actual notice inasmuch as they failed to establish that they were unaware of the water in the location of plaintiff’s accident prior to her fall

We further conclude that defendants failed to meet their burden with respect to constructive notice inasmuch as their submissions raise issues of fact whether the wet floor “was visible and apparent and existed for a sufficient length of time prior to plaintiff’s fall to permit [defendants’] employees to discover and remedy it”

orders.description: Defendants’ appeal from the order entered on or about August 31, 2018 denying dismissal.
orders.trial_court_action: Denied defendants’ motion for summary judgment dismissing the complaint.

facts.factual_summary: Plaintiff allegedly slipped on a wet substance on interior stairs in defendants’ building. He testified that the stairs were dry when he first left, that he saw wetness on returning a short while later but told no one, and that he fell while leaving a second time.

legal_issues.finding: The court applied a reasonable-cleaning-routine rule: the incident occurred outside the scheduled routine, and plaintiff raised no factual issue that the routine was manifestly unreasonable and required alteration.
The court held plaintiff’s testimony demonstrated defendants lacked actual notice; plaintiff said he did not notify anyone after observing the wet condition.
The court held plaintiff’s account showed insufficient time for discovery/remedy and therefore no constructive notice. The elapsed time is described only as a short while, without a numeric interval.

evidence_discussed.description: Superintendent testified to the janitorial schedule for a particular day; the court accepted the reasonable routine analysis. No written schedule or maintenance log is expressly identified.
Plaintiff testified to the dry stairs on his first departure, wetness on return, lack of notification and fall on a second departure; the court relied on this account for both notice grounds.

quality.notes: Generic defendants’ building, superintendent testimony and the housing-development defendant’s name do not expressly establish private ownership/control of the actual premises under the initial rules. Building subtype, plaintiff’s tenant/visitor status, exact property roles and accident date remain unknown. Wet substance is other, not inferred water. Reversal grants defense dismissal and favors defendants, but the label is null pending property review. Plaintiff’s prior observation is not independently analyzed as open-and-obvious, assumption of risk or comparative fault. No creation ruling is supplied; no documentary cleaning record is inferred from schedule testimony.

evidence.quote: Order, Supreme Court, Bronx County (Donna Mills, J.), entered on or about August 31, 2018, which denied defendants' motion for summary judgment dismissing the complaint, unanimously reversed, on the law, without costs, and the motion granted. The Clerk is directed to enter judgment accordingly.
Summary judgment should have been granted in this action where plaintiff alleges that he was injured when he slipped and fell on a wet substance on the interior stairs of defendants' building.
Defendants' superintendent offered testimony as to the janitorial schedule to be followed on a particular day.
An established reasonable cleaning routine precludes the imposition of liability

Where, as here, the incident occurs outside of the scheduled cleaning routine, plaintiff's failure to raise a factual issue that such routine was manifestly unreasonable so as to require altering it warrants dismissal of the complaint

Furthermore, plaintiff testified that there was no wet condition on the stairs when he left the building, that upon his return a short while later he observed an alleged wet condition on the stairs, that he did not notify anyone of such condition, and that as a result of this condition he slipped and fell on the stairs as he was leaving the building a second time.

Plaintiff's testimony demonstrates that defendants did not have actual notice of the purported wet condition, or constructive notice given that the condition did not exist for a sufficient length of time prior to the accident to permit defendants' employees to discover and remedy it

orders.description: Defendants’ appeal from the order entered on or about March 26, 2018 denying dismissal.
orders.trial_court_action: Denied defendants’ motion for summary judgment dismissing the complaint.

facts.factual_summary: Plaintiff allegedly slipped on liquid on interior stairs of an apartment building owned by 1386 Associates and managed by SDG Management. She testified that she reached for a loose handrail and fell; the superintendent described a prior clamp repair in that area with one required screw broken.

legal_issues.finding: Defendants established noncreation prima facie as to the alleged liquid. This finding does not resolve the separate handrail theory, on which their initial burden failed.
Defendants established lack of actual notice prima facie as to the alleged liquid. This finding does not resolve the separate handrail theory, on which their initial burden failed.
Defendants established lack of constructive notice prima facie as to the alleged liquid. This finding does not resolve the separate handrail theory, on which their initial burden failed.

Defendants failed to establish entitlement to dismissal of the alternative defective-handrail theory because the superintendent described an earlier clamp repair with one of four required screws broken. The court did not finally find the handrail defective or apportion liability.

evidence_discussed.description: Plaintiff testified that she tried to grab the handrail when slipping, but it was loose.

Superintendent’s deposition described repairing the relevant handrail with a clamp, with one of four required screws broken; that testimony defeated defendants’ initial showing on the handrail theory.

quality.notes: Actual apartment-building ownership and management are explicit. Liquid is unspecified and coded other. Injured role and accident date are unstated. Defendants’ successful initial liquid showing and unsuccessful handrail showing yield a single full affirmance, not a mixed disposition. The opinion does not assign the handrail failure to a particular creation/notice doctrine; it is captured under other rather than treating the broken-screw testimony as a conclusive finding of actual notice or negligent creation. No code violation, expert proof or separate causation-identification analysis is stated.

evidence.quote: Order, Supreme Court, Bronx County (Elizabeth A. Taylor, J.), entered on or about March 26, 2018, which denied defendants' motion for summary judgment dismissing the complaint, unanimously affirmed, without costs.
Plaintiff alleges that she slipped and fell on a slippery liquid on the interior stairs of an apartment building owned by defendant 1386 Associates, LLC, and managed by defendant SDG Management Corp.
Plaintiff testified that when she began to slip, she reached for the stairs' handrail, but it was loose, and she fell.
Defendants met their prima facie burden of showing that they neither created, nor had actual or constructive notice of, the alleged liquid on the stairway

However, they failed to meet their burden with respect to plaintiff's alternative theory of liability, the allegedly defective handrail, given the superintendent's deposition testimony that he had previously repaired the handrail in the area where plaintiff fell by securing it with a clamp, but that one of the four screws needed to install the clamp was broken

orders.description: Plaintiff’s limited appeal from the September 16, 2014 order granting Walmart Real Estate Business Trust summary judgment.
orders.trial_court_action: Granted Walmart Real Estate Business Trust’s motion dismissing the complaint insofar as asserted against it.

facts.factual_summary: Plaintiff allegedly slipped and fell on premises leased by Walmart Real Estate Business Trust and then subleased to another corporate entity. The opinion does not identify the accident area, hazard or premises use.

legal_issues.finding: Walmart, as lessee/sublessor, failed to show the sublessee assumed exclusive maintenance responsibility and that Walmart had no maintenance duty. The court did not conclusively allocate that duty or find negligence.

Applying out-of-possession principles to a lessee/sublessor, the court found Walmart had not established the exclusive maintenance transfer necessary for dismissal; the plaintiff’s opposition sufficiency was immaterial.

quality.notes: The source expressly places the fall on leased/subleased premises, supporting private leased property without relying only on a corporate name. Defendant_roles tenant/other captures lessee/sublessor; ownership is not inferred. Premises subtype, precise location, hazard, injured role and accident date are unknown; Walmart’s name does not establish a retail store. The general rule discusses contractual/statutory duties but no specific code violation is asserted. Although lease relationships are stated, no particular submitted lease instrument or other evidence format is identified. The caption’s third-party action is not the issue decided. The full appealed portion of one order is reversed, label 1, without dismissing the negligence claim.

evidence.quote: Ordered that the order is reversed insofar as appealed from, on the law, with costs, and the motion of the defendant Walmart Real Estate Business Trust for summary judgment dismissing the complaint insofar as asserted against it is denied.

The plaintiff commenced this action after he allegedly was injured when he slipped and fell on premises that had been leased by the defendant Walmart Real Estate Business Trust (hereinafter the defendant), and then subleased to another corporate entity.

In an action to recover damages for personal injuries, the plaintiff appeals, as limited by his brief, from so much of an order of the Supreme Court, Suffolk County (Pitts, J.), dated September 16, 2014, as granted the motion of the defendant Walmart Real Estate Business Trust for summary judgment dismissing the complaint insofar as asserted against it.

Here, viewing the evidence in the light most favorable to the plaintiff, the defendant [*2] failed to establish, prima facie, that the nonparty sublessee assumed the exclusive obligation to maintain the premises, and that the defendant, as the lessee/sublessor, had no duty to maintain the premises
Since the defendant failed to meet its initial burden as the movant, it is not necessary to review the sufficiency of the plaintiff's opposition papers
Accordingly, the Supreme Court should have denied the defendant's motion for summary judgment dismissing the complaint insofar as asserted against it.

"[A]n out-of-possession landlord may be liable for injuries occurring on the premises if 'it has retained control of the premises, is contractually obligated to perform maintenance and repairs, or is obligated by statute to perform such maintenance and repairs' "

However, "where the premises have been leased and subleased and the subtenant assumes the exclusive obligation to maintain the premises, both the out-of-possession landlord and the out-of-possession lessee/sublessor will be free from liability for injuries to a third party caused by the negligence of the subtenant in possession"

orders.description: Plaintiff’s appeal from the June 27, 2022 judgment entered on the May 24, 2022 summary-judgment order.
orders.trial_court_action: Entered judgment for defendant dismissing the complaint upon the grant of defendant’s summary-judgment motion.

facts.factual_summary: Plaintiff allegedly slipped and fell on an interior staircase in defendant’s apartment building. The specific alleged hazard is not described in the opinion, and plaintiff could not identify what caused her fall without speculation.

legal_issues.finding: Defendant established through plaintiff’s deposition that she could not identify the cause without speculation. Plaintiff raised no triable issue, and her expert report also failed to connect its alleged hazard to the fall.
Plaintiff’s expert report was inadmissible in form without an offered excuse. Independently, it was insufficient to raise a triable issue of proximate causation even if considered.
The court rejected the expert report’s inadmissible form and lack of excuse, citing CPLR 2106; it separately found the report substantively insufficient on causation.

evidence_discussed.description: Defendant submitted plaintiff’s deposition, which demonstrated inability to identify the cause without speculation.
Plaintiff’s expert report was in inadmissible form and independently insufficient on proximate causation. The expert’s discipline, the specific condition and the precise formal defect are unstated.

quality.notes: Private apartment-building ownership and a slip are explicit. Failed causal identification does not exclude an otherwise eligible fall. Hazard, injured role and accident date are unknown; no code violation is inferred from an unnamed expert-identified condition. This is a substantive negligence decision despite the ancillary report-admissibility ground. The opinion does not specify whether the report was unsworn or identify another exact formal defect. Only the June judgment is appealed; its underlying May order is history, not a second appealed order. Preliminary test-period opinion: unchanged rules applied without tuning.

evidence.quote: Ordered that the judgment is affirmed, with costs.
The plaintiff allegedly was injured when she slipped and fell on an interior staircase of an apartment building, which was owned by the defendant.

In an action to recover damages for personal injuries, the plaintiff appeals from a judgment of the Supreme Court, Queens County (Mojgan C. Lancman, J.), entered June 27, 2022. The judgment, upon an order of the same court dated May 24, 2022, granting the defendant's motion for summary judgment dismissing the complaint, is in favor of the defendant and against the plaintiff dismissing the complaint.

The defendant established its prima facie entitlement to judgment as a matter of law by submitting the deposition testimony of the plaintiff, which demonstrated that she could not identify what had caused her to fall without engaging in speculation
In opposition, the plaintiff failed to raise a triable issue of fact.
The report of the plaintiff's expert was not in admissible form, and the plaintiff offered no excuse for failing to tender the report in admissible form
In any event, the report was insufficient to raise a triable issue of fact as to whether the alleged hazardous condition identified therein was a proximate cause of the plaintiff's fall
Accordingly, the judgment is affirmed.
